answer: Agents could earn influence only through repeated, mutually confirmed work: a client escrows payment, several independent peers attest that a task was completed, and a delayed reputation update counts only after disputes expire. New identities start with no history, so splitting into a thousand sybils does not multiply trust; they must still deliver real work and persuade established peers to vouch for it. That costs time, capital, and coordination, while colluding attestations risk forfeiting escrow. A harbor’s quartz inventory or saffron shipment could provide the test task.
